_comment: Metadata for the wasm demo gallery. build-pages.py discovers demos by scanning the built bin/ for <demo>.wasm; anything listed here gets rich text, anything NOT listed still appears with name-based defaults. 'order' controls gallery ordering (listed first, discovered extras appended). WASM_MB is computed from the built file, not stored here.

lsystem_forest.desc: a procedural L-system island with wind, sea and ray-cast cloud volumes
lsystem_forest.blurb: Fly over a procedural island: L-system trees swaying in the wind, a travelling-wave sea and a GPU ray-cast cloud volume, with shadow maps and a free orbit/fly camera. 100% procedural — nothing is downloaded.

lsystem_coast.desc: a procedural coastline with a GPU FFT ocean and breaking surf
lsystem_coast.blurb: Sail a procedural coastline where a GPU FFT ocean rolls in: an FFT-synthesised wave spectrum evolved live on the GPU, an L-system shore, sky and sun, with a free orbit/fly camera. 100% procedural — nothing is downloaded.

nav_city_swarm.desc: the GRL-SNAM reactive swarm on a procedural city
nav_city_swarm.blurb: 800 vehicles cross a foggy city with no global plan — the GRL-SNAM reactive swarm on the cvc::nav runtime (no Python, no libtorch). Tune agents, fog and belief live, then Apply / Restart to watch shared belief beat private belief on the same city.

nav_fog_ghost.desc: one agent detours a phantom wall, then senses it clear
nav_fog_ghost.blurb: Fog of war: a vehicle detours a phantom wall its stale map shows but reality lacks, then erases it cell by cell as its sensor clears the ground. Switch between three limited-belief scenarios — ghost, dynamic and traffic.

volren_bunny.desc: the Stanford bunny as a signed-distance volume, CPU-raycast live
volren_bunny.blurb: Two bunnies, two renderers: the classic mesh beside a signed-distance-field volume of the same bunny, raycast on the CPU by cvc::volren and composited into the scene with a per-pixel depth map — watch it occlude and be occluded as it spins. The SDF is computed live from the mesh at startup; the raycast image, its translucent shell and the raster resolution are all software, no GPU volume tricks.

bunny_shadow.desc: the Stanford bunny under an aimed spot — shadow mapping, up close
bunny_shadow.blurb: The smallest scene that tests a renderer honestly: one known-good mesh on a ground plane under a StageLighting rig. Shadow-map artefacts have nowhere to hide here — acne, peter-panning and a shadow in the wrong place are all obvious on a single caster. Toggle shadows and the lighting panel to watch a tight spot cone spend its texels where a directional light would waste them.
